units.zh: 夫乾坤定位，男女流形，伉儷之義同歸，貴賤之名異等。
units.en: Heaven and earth fixed their stations; men and women took their bodily shapes. Husband and wife share one moral purpose, even though rank divides high from low.
units.literal: As for Qian and Kun taking their positions, male and female receive their forms; the principle of husband and wife aims at the same end, yet the names of noble and base stand in different ranks.

units.zh: 若乃作配皇極，齊體紫宸，象玉床之連後星，喻金波之合羲璧。
units.en: Those who match the sovereign on high and share the body politic of the inner palace are figured as the jade couch tied to the queen’s asterism, as moonlight married to the solar disk.
units.literal: When one is paired with the supreme apex and shares the substance of the Purple Palace, it is likened to the jade couch linking to the rear stars, and compared to golden waves joining the Xi disk.

units.zh: 爰自敻古，是謂元妃；
units.en: In deepest antiquity she was known as the principal wife;
units.literal: From remote antiquity onward, she was called the chief consort;

units.zh: 降及中年，乃稱王后。
units.en: Later ages styled her queen.
units.literal: Descending to middle antiquity, she was then titled queen.

units.zh: 四人並列，光于帝嚳之宮；
units.en: Four consorts stood side by side and brought glory to Emperor Ku’s inner court;
units.literal: Four women stood ranked together, shining in the palace of Emperor Ku;

units.zh: 二妃同降，著彼有虞之典。
units.en: Two royal brides arrived together and entered the canonical record of Shun’s reign.
units.literal: Two consorts descended together, written into the canons of Yu’s age.

units.zh: 夏商以上，六宮之制，其詳靡得而聞焉。
units.en: For ages before Xia and Shang, no reliable detail survives about how the six wings of the harem were ordered.
units.literal: Above Xia and Shang, the regulations of the Six Palaces cannot be heard of in detail.

units.zh: 姬劉以降，五翟之規，其事可略而言矣。
units.en: From the Zhou and Han dynasties on, the graded “five pheasant” ritual for consorts can at least be sketched.
units.literal: From Ji and Liu onward, the rules of the five pheasant insignia may be spoken of in outline.

units.zh: 周禮，天子立一后、三夫人、九嬪、二十七世婦、八十一御妻，以聽王者內政。
units.en: The Rites of Zhou prescribe one empress, three chief consorts, nine ranked ladies, twenty-seven secondary wives, and eighty-one attendants to manage the sovereign’s domestic government.
units.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Son of Heaven establishes one queen, three ladies, nine bin, twenty-seven wives of rank, and eighty-one minor wives, to administer the king’s inner administration.

units.zh: 故婚義曰：「天子之與后，如日之與月，陰之與陽。」
units.en: The Meaning of Marriage therefore declares: “The emperor and his empress mirror sun and moon, yin and yang.”
units.literal: Therefore the Meaning of Marriage says: “The Son of Heaven and the queen are like sun and moon, yin and yang.”

units.zh: 由斯而談，其所從來遠矣。
units.en: Judged by such language, their institution reaches far back into antiquity.
units.literal: From this perspective, what they derive from is distant indeed.

units.zh: 故能母儀天宇，助宣王化，德均載物，比大坤維，宗廟歆其薦羞，穹壤俟其交泰。
units.en: Hence she sets the maternal standard for the realm, advances the king’s civilizing work, and bears creation as steadfastly as earth itself; the temple accepts her sacrifices gladly, and heaven and earth look to her union with the throne for peace.
units.literal: Thus she can be the motherly model for all under heaven, aid in spreading royal transformation, her virtue evenly bearing all things, comparable to the great sustaining power of Kun; the ancestral temple delights in her offerings, heaven and earth await her harmonizing union.

units.zh: 是以哲王垂憲，尤重造舟之禮；
units.en: That is why enlightened monarchs codify law and prize above all the royal wedding rite of “meeting across the boat.”
units.literal: Therefore wise kings hang forth statutes and especially esteem the rite of the built bridge;

units.zh: 詩人立言，先獎葛覃之訓。
units.en: The Classic of Poetry opens by honoring the lessons of “Ge Tan,” the ode on diligent royal ladies.
units.literal: The poets set forth words and first praise the instruction of “Ge Tan.”

units.zh: 後燭流景，所以裁其宴私；
units.en: Dimming the late-night lamp curbs excess in the privy chamber;
units.literal: The rear candle’s flowing light is the means to regulate their private banquets;

units.zh: 房樂希聲，是用節其容止。
units.en: Sparse music in the inner rooms reins in conduct at court and couch alike.
units.literal: Chamber music with sparse sound is the means to moderate their bearing.

units.zh: 履端正本，抑斯之謂歟！
units.en: Walking straight to set the root right—surely this is what those measures intend!
units.literal: Walking upright to rectify the root—is this not what is meant!

units.zh: 若乃娉納有方，防閑有禮，肅尊儀而修四德，體柔範而弘六義，陰教洽于宮闈，淑譽騰於區域。
units.en: When matches are arranged by rule, propriety fences passion, majesty guards ritual while the four womanly virtues are cultivated, gentle models enlarge the six canonical lessons, inner-chamber teaching fills the harem, and fair fame spreads beyond the capital.
units.literal: If betrothal and intake have proper method, fences and restraint have ritual, reverently honoring ceremony while cultivating the four virtues, embodying gentle norms while extending the six meanings, then women’s instruction permeates the palace, and good reputation rises through the regions.

units.zh: 則玄雲入戶，上帝錫母萌之符；
units.en: Then auspicious clouds cross the threshold and Heaven grants the token of fruitful motherhood;
units.literal: Then dark clouds enter the door, and the Supreme Lord grants the sign of motherhood’s sprouting;

units.zh: 黃神降徵，坤靈贊壽丘之道，終能鼎祚惟永，胤嗣克昌。
units.en: The divine Yellow Emperor sends portents; earth’s spirit blesses the birth-hill of sage-kings; the dynasty’s mandate endures and heirs thrive.
units.literal: The Yellow Spirit sends down omens; the spirit of Kun assists the way of Shouqiu; ultimately the tripod fortune can be everlasting and heirs flourish.

units.zh: 至若儷極虧閑，憑天作孽，倒裳衣于衽席，感朓側於弦望。
units.en: But women who reach the throne yet abandon modesty, who invoke Heaven while plotting harm, who turn proper dress upside down on the bed, and whose passions shift with every phase of the moon—
units.literal: As for those paired to the apex yet deficient in restraint, who rely on heaven to work calamity, who overturn upper and lower garments upon the mat, and feel lust askew at first quarter and full moon.

units.zh: 則龍漦結釁，宗周鞠為黍苗；
units.en: —dragon spit seals a fatal feud, and the Zhou heartland turns to weed-grown ruin;
units.literal: Then dragon-spittle knots disaster, and royal Zhou becomes nothing but millet shoots;

units.zh: 燕尾挻災，隆漢墜其枌社矣。
units.en: swallow-tail charms invite catastrophe, and even mighty Han loses its soil-and-millet shrines.
units.literal: Swallow tails draw calamity, and flourishing Han drops its mulberry altars.

units.zh: 自曹劉內主，位以色登，甄衛之家，榮非德舉。
units.en: Under the Cao and Liu courts, palace ladies rose by looks alone; clans such as the Zhens and Weis won favor without moral merit.
units.literal: Since the inner mistresses of Cao and Liu, position climbed by beauty; in the households of Zhen and Wei, glory was not raised by virtue.

units.zh: 淫荒挺性，蔑西郊之禮容；
units.en: Wanton temperaments mocked the solemn suburban liturgy reserved for the empress;
units.literal: Dissolute and wasteful by nature, they slighted the ritual bearing of the western suburb;

units.zh: 婉孌含辭，作南國之奇態。
units.en: Soft voices and studied phrases invented the freakish grace of southern entertainers.
units.literal: Soft loveliness holding coy phrases, they fashioned exotic manners of the southern states.

units.zh: 詖謁由斯外人，穢德於是內宣。
units.en: Sycophancy leaked beyond the palace gates while depravity was preached inside.
units.literal: Slanderous flattery thereby passed outward, and foul conduct was proclaimed within.

units.zh: 椒掖播晨牝之風，蘭殿絕河雎之響。
units.en: The harem aired the omen of women ruling like crowing hens; orchid halls no longer echoed the chaste songs of “Guan ju.”
units.literal: The pepper chambers spread the wind of the hen crowing at dawn; the orchid halls cut off the echo of “Guan ju” by the River.

units.zh: 永言彤史，大練之範逾微；
units.en: Forever the palace diarists wrote, yet the ideal of homespun austerity faded;
units.literal: Speaking long of the vermilion scribe, the model of coarse white silk grows ever fainter;

units.zh: 緬視青蒲，脫珥之猷替矣。
units.en: Looking back to mat audiences where consorts remonstrated, the counsel of tearing off earrings to warn the throne had vanished.
units.literal: Gazing afar at the green rushes, the strategy of casting off ear-jewels is replaced.

units.zh: 晉承其末，與世污隆，宣皇創基，功弘而道屈；
units.en: The Jin took up this fallen era and rose or fell with the times. Emperor Xuan laid the foundations: his deeds were grand, yet the moral course stayed cramped;
units.literal: Jin inherited the late age; with the world it sank and rose. Emperor Xuan founded the base—achievement broad yet the Way bent;

units.zh: 穆后一善，勣侔於十亂。
units.en: a single virtue in Empress Mu rivaled the merit of the ten capable ministers who ordered the realm.
units.literal: one goodness of Empress Mu—merit equal to the ten capable ministers.

units.zh: 洎乎世祖，[1]始親選良家，既而帝掩紈扇，躬行請託。
units.en: Under Emperor Wu [1] the court at first picked brides from respectable houses; soon the sovereign waved his silk fan in the inner quarters and himself traded favors for appointments.
units.literal: Down to Shizu [1], he began personally selecting from good families; thereafter the emperor hid behind the silk fan and personally practiced solicitation.

units.zh: 后採長白，實彰妒忌之情；
units.en: An empress chosen for graying hair laid bare the spite of jealousy;
units.literal: The empress chose “long white,” truly displaying jealousy;

units.zh: 賈納短青，竟踐覆亡之轍。
units.en: the Jias welcomed a young rival and eventually followed the same rut to ruin.
units.literal: Jia took in “short green,” and in the end trod the rut of overthrow.

units.zh: 得失遺跡，煥在綈緗，興滅所由，義同畫一。
units.en: Success and failure still gleam from the silk-bound histories; the springs of fortune and disaster follow one clear pattern.
units.literal: Tracks of gain and loss shine forth on silk documents; the causes of rise and ruin share one uniform pattern in meaning.

units.zh: 故列其本事，以為后妃傳云。
units.en: I therefore set out the essential facts as this “Treatise on Empresses and Consorts.”
units.literal: Therefore I array their basic affairs to form this treatise on empresses and consorts.

units.zh: 宣穆張皇后
units.en: Empress Zhang the August and Revered
units.literal: Empress Zhang Xuanmu

units.zh: 宣穆張皇后諱春華，河內平皋人也。
units.en: Empress Zhang Xuanmu, personal name Chunhua, came from Pinggao in Henei commandery.
units.literal: Empress Zhang Xuanmu, taboo name Chunhua, was a native of Pinggao in Henei.

units.zh: 父汪，魏粟邑令；
units.en: Her father Wang had served as magistrate of Suyi under Wei;
units.literal: Her father Wang was magistrate of Suyi in Wei;

units.zh: 母河內山氏，司徒濤之從祖姑也。
units.en: her mother was a Shan from Henei, a paternal grand-aunt by cousinship of Minister over the Masses Shan Tao.
units.literal: her mother was a Shan of Henei, a paternal grand-aunt by cousinship of Minister over the Masses Shan Tao.

units.zh: 后少有德行，智識過人，生景帝、文帝、平原王幹、南陽公主。
units.en: She showed virtue and unusual discernment from girlhood. She was mother to Emperors Jing and Wen, to Prince Sima Gan of Pingyuan, and to the Princess of Nanyang.
units.literal: The empress from youth had virtuous conduct and intelligence surpassing others; she bore Emperor Jing, Emperor Wen, Prince Gan of Pingyuan, and the Princess of Nanyang.

units.zh: 宣帝初辭魏武之命，託以風痹，嘗暴書，遇暴雨，不覺自起收之。
units.en: When Emperor Xuan first refused Cao Cao’s summons, claiming crippling palsy, he once aired books in the sun. A cloudburst came; forgetting his act, he leapt up to rescue them.
units.literal: When Emperor Xuan at first declined Wei Wu’s summons, pleading wind paralysis, he once sunned books; encountering a sudden storm, unthinkingly he rose himself to gather them in.

units.zh: 家惟有一婢見之，后乃恐事泄致禍，遂手殺之以滅口，而親自執爨。
units.en: A single bondmaid witnessed it. Fearing exposure would destroy them, the empress killed her with her own hands and herself cooked the family meals to hide the truth.
units.literal: Only one maid in the house saw it; the empress then feared the affair leaking and bringing disaster, so she personally killed her to silence her, and herself attended the cooking stove.

units.zh: 帝由是重之。
units.en: Thereafter her husband valued her all the more.
units.literal: The emperor from this esteemed her.

units.zh: 其後柏夫人有寵，后罕得進見。
units.en: Later Lady Bai won his favor, and the empress was seldom admitted.
units.literal: Afterward Lady Bai had favor, and the empress rarely obtained audience.

units.zh: 帝嘗臥疾，后往省病。
units.en: Once when he lay sick, she came to nurse him.
units.literal: The emperor once lay ill; the empress went to inquire after his illness.

units.zh: 帝曰：「老物可憎，何煩出也！」
units.en: He snapped, “That foul old hag—why drag herself here!”
units.literal: The emperor said: “That old creature is hateful—why trouble to come out!”

units.zh: 后慚恚不食，將自殺，諸子亦不食。
units.en: Shamed and furious, she refused food and meant to take her life; her sons fasted with her.
units.literal: The empress, ashamed and enraged, did not eat and was about to kill herself; her sons likewise did not eat.

units.zh: 帝驚而致謝，后乃止。
units.en: Alarmed, he apologized, and she gave up the attempt.
units.literal: The emperor was alarmed and apologized; the empress then stopped.

units.zh: 帝退而謂人曰：「老物不足惜，慮困我好兒耳！」
units.en: Privately he muttered, “I care nothing for the hag—I fear only harm to my fine sons.”
units.literal: The emperor withdrew and said to someone: “The old creature is not worth pity—I worry she will distress my good sons!”

units.zh: 魏正始八年崩，時年五十九，葬洛陽高原陵，追贈廣平縣君。
units.en: She died in 247 at fifty-nine and was buried at Gaoyuan mausoleum at Luoyang; Wei later enfeoffed her posthumously as Lady of Guangping.
units.literal: She died in Wei’s eighth Zhengshi year, aged fifty-nine, buried at Gaoyuan tumulus in Luoyang, posthumously endowed as Lady of Guangping County.

units.zh: 咸熙元年，追號宣穆妃。
units.en: In 264 she received the posthumous title Consort Xuanmu.
units.literal: In the first Xianxi year she was posthumously titled Consort Xuanmu.

units.zh: 及武帝受禪，追尊為皇后。
units.en: When Emperor Wu took the throne, she was raised posthumously to empress.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, she was posthumously honored as empress.

units.zh: 景懷夏侯皇后
units.en: Empress Xiahou the Revered and Cherished
units.literal: Empress Xiahou Jinghuai

units.zh: 景懷夏侯皇后諱徽，字媛容，沛國譙人也。
units.en: Empress Xiahou Jinghuai, personal name Hui, courtesy name Yuanrong, came from Qiao in the state of Pei.
units.literal: Empress Xiahou Jinghuai, taboo name Hui, courtesy name Yuanrong, was a native of Qiao in Pei.

units.zh: 父尚，魏征南大將軍；
units.en: Her father Xiahou Shang held Wei’s post of Grand General Who Conquers the South;
units.literal: Her father Shang was Grand General Who Conquers the South in Wei;

units.zh: 母曹氏，魏德陽鄉主。
units.en: her mother was a daughter of the Wei imperial house, titled Village Mistress of Deyang.
units.literal: her mother was a Cao, Village Mistress of Deyang in Wei.

units.zh: 后雅有識度，帝每有所為，必豫籌畫。
units.en: She was poised and far-sighted; whatever her husband planned, she anticipated and shaped.
units.literal: The empress elegantly had insight and measure; whenever the emperor had something to do, she always planned ahead.

units.zh: 魏明帝世，宣帝居上將之重，諸子並有雄才大略。
units.en: Under Wei Mingdi, Sima Yi commanded the armies while his sons all had heroic talent and grand strategic vision.
units.literal: In Emperor Ming of Wei’s reign, Emperor Xuan occupied the weight of supreme commander; his sons all had heroic talent and broad strategies.

units.zh: 后知帝非魏之純臣，而后既魏氏之甥，帝深忌之。
units.en: She knew Sima Yi was no loyal servant of Wei, yet as a maternal niece of the Wei ruling house she herself drew his deepest suspicion.
units.literal: The empress knew the emperor was not a pure minister of Wei, yet the empress was moreover a niece of the Wei clan—deeply the emperor suspected her.

units.zh: 青龍二年，遂以鴆崩，時年二十四，葬峻平陵。
units.en: In 234 she was poisoned at twenty-four and buried at Junping mausoleum.
units.literal: In the second Qinglong year she then died by poisoned wine, aged twenty-four, buried at Junping tumulus.

units.zh: 武帝登阼，初未追崇，弘訓太后每以為言，泰始二年始加號諡。
units.en: After Emperor Wu took the throne he left her unhonored until Empress Dowager Yang at Hongxun repeatedly pressed the matter; only in 266 did he grant posthumous rank and epithet.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, at first he did not posthumously honor her; Empress Dowager Hongxun often spoke of it; only in the second Taishi year did he begin adding title and posthumous name.

units.zh: 后無男，生五女。
units.en: She had no sons but five daughters.
units.literal: The empress had no sons; she bore five daughters.

units.zh: 景獻羊皇后
units.en: Empress Yang the Revered and Offered
units.literal: Empress Yang Jingxian

units.zh: 景獻羊皇后諱徽瑜，泰山南城人。
units.en: Empress Yang Jingxian, personal name Huiyu, came from Nancheng in Taishan commandery.
units.literal: Empress Yang Jingxian, taboo name Huiyu, was a person of Nancheng in Taishan.

units.zh: 父茞，上黨太守；
units.en: Her father Yang Zhi served as governor of Shangdang;
units.literal: Her father Zhi was governor of Shangdang;

units.zh: 后母陳留蔡氏，漢左中郎將邕之女也。
units.en: her mother was a Cai from Chenliu, daughter of the Han General of the Household of the Left Cai Yong.
units.literal: the empress’s mother was a Cai of Chenliu, daughter of Han’s Left General of the Household Cai Yong.

units.zh: 后聰敏有才行。
units.en: She was quick-witted, talented, and principled.
units.literal: The empress was clever, keen, and had talent and conduct.

units.zh: 景懷皇后崩，景帝更娶鎮北將軍濮陽吳質女，見黜，復納后，無子。
units.en: After Empress Xiahou died, Emperor Jing married the daughter of Wu Zhi of Puyang, General Who Guards the North; she was dismissed, and he then married Yang Huiyu; she bore no sons.
units.literal: When Empress Jinghuai died, Emperor Jing further married the daughter of Wu Zhi of Puyang, General Who Guards the North; she was dismissed; he then took in the empress; she had no sons.

units.zh: 武帝受禪，居弘訓宮，號弘訓太后。
units.en: When Emperor Wu assumed the throne she moved to Hongxun Palace as dowager.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, she resided in Hongxun Palace, titled Empress Dowager Hongxun.

units.zh: 泰始九年，追贈蔡氏濟陽縣君，諡曰穆。
units.en: In 273 her mother was posthumously named Lady of Jiyang with the epithet Mu.
units.literal: In the ninth Taishi year Lady Cai was posthumously endowed as Mistress of Jiyang County, posthumous name Mu.

units.zh: 咸寧四年，太后崩，時年六十五，祔葬峻平陵。
units.en: She died in 278 at sixty-five and was interred beside Emperor Jing at Junping.
units.literal: In the fourth Xianning year the empress dowager died, aged sixty-five, buried by accompaniment at Junping tumulus.

units.zh: 文明王皇后
units.en: Empress Wang the Cultured and Illustrious
units.literal: Empress Wang Wenming

units.zh: 文明王皇后諱元姬，東海郯人也。
units.en: Empress Wang Wenming, personal name Yuanji, came from Tan in Donghai commandery.
units.literal: Empress Wang Wenming, taboo name Yuanji, was a native of Tan in Donghai.

units.zh: 父肅，魏中領軍、蘭陵侯。
units.en: Her father Wang Su served Wei as Central Commandant and Marquis of Lanling.
units.literal: Her father Su was Central Commandant of the Army in Wei, Marquis of Lanling.

units.zh: 后年八歲，誦詩論，尤善喪服；
units.en: At eight she could recite the Odes and Analects and had mastered the ritual chapters on mourning dress;
units.literal: At age eight the empress recited the Odes and Analects and was especially good at mourning garments;

units.zh: 苟有文義，目所一見，必貫於心。
units.en: whatever text she read once lodged permanently in memory.
units.literal: if there was textual meaning, what her eyes once saw, she must thread through her heart.

units.zh: 年九歲，遇母疾，扶侍不捨左右，衣不解帶者久之。
units.en: At nine, when her mother fell ill, she nursed her night and day without loosening her sash for weeks.
units.literal: At age nine, encountering her mother’s illness, she attended without leaving her side, not undoing her belt for clothing for a long time.

units.zh: 每先意候指，動中所適，由是父母令攝家事，每盡其理。
units.en: She anticipated every wish so deftly that her parents put her in charge of the household, which she ran flawlessly.
units.literal: Always anticipating intention and watching for hints, her actions hit what was fitting; therefore her parents ordered her to manage household affairs, and she always exhausted reason in them.

units.zh: 祖朗甚愛異之，曰：「興吾家者，必此女也，惜不為男矣！」
units.en: Her grandfather Wang Lang doted on her, saying, “This girl will redeem our line—if only she were a son!”
units.literal: Her grandfather Lang greatly loved and regarded her as unusual, saying: “The one who will raise our house must be this girl—alas that she is not a boy!”

units.zh: 年十二，朗薨，后哀戚哭泣，發于自然，其父益加敬異。
units.en: When Wang Lang died she was twelve; her grief was utterly spontaneous, and her father prized her even more.
units.literal: At twelve Lang died; the empress mourned and wept in grief, arising from the natural; her father increasingly respected her as unusual.

units.zh: 既笄，歸于文帝，生武帝及遼東悼王定國、齊獻王攸、城陽哀王兆、廣漢殤王廣德、京兆公主。
units.en: After coming of age she married Sima Zhao (later Emperor Wen) and bore Sima Yan (Emperor Wu), Princes Dingguo, You, Zhao, and Guangde, and the Princess of Jingzhao.
units.literal: After capping-age she married Emperor Wen and bore Emperor Wu, Prince Dingguo of Liaodong, Prince You of Qi, Prince Zhao of Chengyang, Prince Guangde of Guanghan, and the Princess of Jingzhao.

units.zh: 后事舅姑盡婦道，謙沖接下，嬪御有序。
units.en: She observed every duty to her in-laws, treated inferiors with modesty, and kept the inner household in harmony.
units.literal: The empress served parents-in-law exhausting wife’s way, humble and yielding in receiving those below, concubines and attendants having order.

units.zh: 及居父喪，身不勝衣，言與淚俱。
units.en: During her father’s mourning she wasted to skin and bone; every word came with tears.
units.literal: When dwelling in mourning for her father, her body did not fill out her garments; speech and tears together.

units.zh: 時鍾會以才能見任，后每言于帝曰：「會見利忘義，好為事端，寵過必亂，不可大任。」
units.en: Zhong Hui had won power through sheer ability; she often warned Emperor Wen, “Zhong chases profit, courts trouble, and will rebel if favor grows—do not give him real authority.”
units.literal: At the time Zhong Hui was employed for talent and ability; the empress often said to the emperor: “Hui sees profit and forgets righteousness, likes to make incidents; favor passed must bring chaos—he cannot be greatly entrusted.”

units.zh: 會後果反。
units.en: Zhong Hui later rose in rebellion, just as she foretold.
units.literal: Hui afterward indeed rebelled.

units.zh: 武帝受禪，尊為皇太后，宮曰崇化。
units.en: When Emperor Wu took the throne she became empress dowager, with residence in Chonghua Palace.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, she was honored as empress dowager; the palace was called Chonghua.

units.zh: 初置宮卿，重選其職，以太常諸葛緒為衛尉，太僕劉原為太僕，宗正曹楷為少府。
units.en: She established palace ministries with careful appointments: Zhuge Xu as minister of the guard, Liu Yuan as grand coachman, Cao Kai as privy treasurer.
units.literal: At first palace ministers were installed; their offices were heavily selected—Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhuge Xu as Commandant of the Guard, Grand Coachman Liu Yuan as Grand Coachman, Director of the Imperial Clan Cao Kai as Privy Treasurer.

units.zh: 后雖處尊位，不忘素業，躬執紡績，器服無文，御浣濯之衣，食不參味。
units.en: Though dowager, she still spun and wove, wore undyed cloth and laundered robes, and took simple meals without mixed dishes.
units.literal: Although the empress occupied an honored position, she did not forget her plain work; personally she held spinning and weaving; vessels and garments had no pattern; she employed washed clothing; food did not mix flavors.

units.zh: 而敦睦九族，垂心萬物，言必典禮，浸潤不行。
units.en: She cherished every branch of kin, cared for all living things, spoke only in classical idiom, and never let private bias seep into policy.
units.literal: Yet she treated the nine kindreds warmly, let her heart hang over all things; speech always followed canon and ritual; seeping influence did not proceed.

units.zh: 帝以后母羊氏未崇諡號，泰始三年下詔曰：「昔漢文追崇靈文之號，武、宣有平原、博平之封，咸所以奉尊尊之敬，廣親親之恩也。
units.en: Because his mother-in-law lacked posthumous honors, Emperor Wu issued in 267 an edict: “Han Wendi conferred the posthumous title Lingwen; Emperors Wu and Xuan of Han granted the fiefs of Pingyuan and Boping—such acts honor parents and widen kinship grace.
units.literal: The emperor because the empress’s mother the Yang clan had not been honored with posthumous title, in the third Taishi year issued an edict saying: “Formerly Han Wen posthumously elevated the title of Lingwen; Wu and Xuan had enfeoffments of Pingyuan and Boping—all were means to serve respect to the honored and widen kindness to kin.

units.zh: 故衛將軍、蘭陵景侯夫人羊氏，含章體順，仁德醇備，內承世冑，出嬪大國，三從之行，率禮無違。
units.en: Lady Yang, widow of Wang Su, the General Who Guards the Army and Marquis Jing of Lanling, bore inward grace and outward modesty, fulfilled every womanly virtue, linked great houses by marriage, and observed the three obediences without fault.
units.literal: Therefore Lady Yang, wife of General Who Guards the Army, Marquis Jing of Lanling, contained pattern and embodied compliance; humane virtue pure and complete; inwardly inheriting generations of lineage, outwardly marrying a great state; in the conduct of the three followings, leading ritual without violation.

units.zh: 仍遭不造，頻喪統嗣，撫育眾胤，克成家道。
units.en: Though Heaven denied her sons and struck down heirs again and again, she raised the wider family and preserved the household.
units.literal: Yet she encountered ill fortune, repeatedly losing heirs who would succeed, fostering many descendants, able to complete family way.

units.zh: 母儀之教，光于邦族，誕啟聖明，祚流萬國。
units.en: Her maternal example illuminated kin and state, opened the way for the sage-sovereign, and spread blessing across every realm.
units.literal: Motherly model instruction shone on state and clan; she broadly opened sagely brightness; fortune flowed to myriad states.

units.zh: 而早世殂隕，不遇休寵。
units.en: Yet she died young before receiving such honors.
units.literal: Yet she died young and fell, not encountering fine favor.

units.zh: 皇太后孝思蒸蒸，永慕罔極。
units.en: The empress dowager mourns her mother with boundless filial love.
units.literal: The empress dowager’s filial thoughts steam upward; forever longing without limit.

units.zh: 朕感存遺訓，追遠傷懷。
units.en: Remembering her teaching, I ache when paying tribute to the past.
units.literal: I am moved to preserve surviving instructions; tracing the distant, injuring the breast.

units.zh: 其封夫人為縣君，依德紀諡，主者詳如舊典。」
units.en: Enfeoff her as a county mistress, grant an epithet suited to her virtue, and let the ministry follow precedent.”
units.literal: Let the lady be enfeoffed as county mistress; according to virtue record posthumous name; those in charge detail according to old canons.”

units.zh: 於是使使持節謁者何融追諡為平陽靖君。
units.en: Envoy He Rong was therefore dispatched with tally and staff to confer posthumously the title Lady Jing of Pingyang.
units.literal: Thereupon envoy bearing staff and insignia, Yeoman He Rong posthumously titled her Pingyang Lady Jing.

units.zh: 四年，后崩，時年五十二，合葬崇陽陵。
units.en: In the fourth year she died at fifty-two and was laid beside him in Chongyang Mausoleum.
units.literal: In the fourth year the empress died. She was fifty-two at death and was buried jointly at Chongyang Mausoleum.

units.zh: 將遷祔，帝手疏后德行，命史官為哀策曰：
units.en: When her cortège was readied for burial at his side, he drafted her virtues in his own hand and told the historiographers to write a lament—thus:
units.literal: When she was to be moved for joint burial, the emperor personally drafted an account of her conduct and ordered the historiographers to compose a dirge of lament, saying:

units.zh: 明明先后，興我晉道。
units.en: Radiant queen who went before, you lifted high our Jin house.
units.literal: O clear-bright late queen, you raised our Jin way.

units.zh: 暉章淑問，以翼皇考。
units.en: Your shining virtue and gracious name steadied our royal father.
units.literal: Your radiant pattern and virtuous fame aided our august father.

units.zh: 邁德宣猷，大業有造。
units.en: You advanced virtue and wise counsel and helped forge the great enterprise.
units.literal: Advancing virtue, spreading counsel—you fashioned the great enterprise.

units.zh: 貽慶孤矇，堂構是保。
units.en: You left blessing to a fatherless heir and preserved the house he would inherit.
units.literal: You left blessing to the orphaned child; you guarded hall and rafters.

units.zh: 庶資復顧，永享難老。
units.en: We hoped still for your shelter and the gift of your undying care.
units.literal: We hoped still to lean on your backward glance and forever enjoy agelessness.

units.zh: 奄然登遐，棄我何早！
units.en: Suddenly you journeyed on—why abandon us this soon!
units.literal: Suddenly you ascended far—why did you leave us so soon!

units.zh: 沈哀罔訴，如何穹昊。
units.en: Grief too deep for words—how shall I cry to boundless Heaven?
units.literal: Deep grief with nowhere to speak—what shall I say to vast Heaven?

units.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
units.en: Alas for this sorrow!
units.literal: Alas, oh grief!

units.zh: 厥初生民，樹之惠康。
units.en: From life’s first dawn kind nurture has sustained the folk.
units.literal: From the first birth of the people, they planted kindness and health.

units.zh: 帝遷明德，顧予先皇。
units.en: Heaven chose a luminous lady to watch beside our late king.
units.literal: The emperor chose bright virtue, watching over our late sovereign.

units.zh: 天立厥配，我皇是光。
units.en: Heaven set her at his side and glorified our throne.
units.literal: Heaven set up his mate; our sovereign was illumined.

units.zh: 作邦作對，德音無疆。
units.en: She matched him as co-ruler; her fair fame knows no shore.
units.literal: She founded the state and formed the pair; her virtuous fame knows no bound.

units.zh: 愍予不弔，天篤降殃。
units.en: Pity your orphaned son—Heaven heaps fresh grief upon him.
units.literal: Pity me unsuccored—Heaven sternly sends calamity.

units.zh: 日沒明夷，中年隕喪。
units.en: The sun dipped into night; in mid-life she was torn away.
units.literal: The sun set in Mingyi’s darkness; mid-years brought collapse.

units.zh: 煢煢在疚，永懷摧傷。
units.en: I stand alone in mourning, heartsick without healing.
units.literal: Alone in affliction, forever cherishing, crushed and wounded.

units.zh: 尋惟景行，於穆不已。
units.en: When I trace her shining conduct, its grandeur knows no end.
units.literal: Tracing her lofty way—ah, majestic without end.

units.zh: 海岱降靈，世荷繁祉。
units.en: Sea and Taishan lent her spirit; age after age received rich blessing.
units.literal: Sea and Mount Tai sent down spirits; generations bore thick blessings.

units.zh: 永錫祚胤，篤生文母。
units.en: Heaven blessed our line with heirs and gave us a mother steeped in pattern.
units.literal: Forever grant heirs and fortune; earnestly was born the cultured mother.

units.zh: 誕膺純和，淑慎容止。
units.en: She bore pure harmony in her blood and moved with modest grace.
units.literal: Born to receive pure harmony, modest and careful in bearing.

units.zh: 質直不渝，體茲孝友。
units.en: Her honesty never wavered; she lived filial love and gentle kindness.
units.literal: Honest and straight, she did not waver; she embodied filial piety and brotherly duty.

units.zh: 詩書是悅，禮籍是紀。
units.en: She delighted in the classics and held the ritual texts as her compass.
units.literal: The Odes and Documents were her delight; ritual canons were her rule.

units.zh: 三從無違，中饋允理。
units.en: She kept the three obediences flawlessly and ordered the inner household aright.
units.literal: The three obediences without fault; the inner kitchen truly ordered.

units.zh: 追惟先后，勞謙是尚。
units.en: Remembering queens past, she prized humble service above all.
units.literal: Tracing the late queens, toil and humility are esteemed.

units.zh: 爰初在室，竭力致養。
units.en: In her girlhood she strained every nerve to care for her parents.
units.literal: When first in the maiden chamber, she exhausted strength to nurture parents.

units.zh: 嬪于大邦，皇基是相。
units.en: She married into a great house and steadied the throne’s foundation.
units.literal: She married into a great state and aided the royal foundation.

units.zh: 謐靜隆化，帝業以創。
units.en: Her quiet grace lifted the realm and gave the dynasty its start.
units.literal: Quiet peace elevated transformation; the imperial enterprise was thereby founded.

units.zh: 內敘嬪御，外協時望。
units.en: Within she schooled the harem; without she answered the hopes of the age.
units.literal: Within she ordered the concubines; without she harmonized the hopes of the age.

units.zh: 履信居順，德行洽暢。
units.en: Faithful in word and compliant in station, her virtue suffused every quarter.
units.literal: Treading faith and dwelling in compliance, virtue and conduct flowed smoothly.

units.zh: 密勿無荒，劬勞克讓。
units.en: She labored without slack and strove with yielding grace.
units.literal: Diligent without negligence, toilsome yet yielding.

units.zh: 崇儉抑華，沖素是放。
units.en: She honored plain cloth over display and made simplicity her fashion.
units.literal: Esteeming thrift and restraining splendor, she took simplicity as her model.

units.zh: 雖享崇高，歡嘉未饗。
units.en: Though raised to the heights, she never tasted idle revelry.
units.literal: Although she enjoyed loftiness, joy and feasting were not yet tasted.

units.zh: 胡寧棄之，我將曷仰？
units.en: How could she leave us—where shall I lift my eyes?
units.literal: How could she leave us—whom shall I look up to?

units.zh: 咨余不造，大罰薦臻。
units.en: Alas for my ill star—Heaven’s blows strike again and again.
units.literal: Alas for my ill fortune—great punishments crowd upon me.

units.zh: 皇考背世，始踰三年。
units.en: My royal father left this world hardly three years ago.
units.literal: Imperial father turned his back on the world—barely three years have passed.

units.zh: 仰奉慈親，冀無後艱。
units.en: I leaned on a loving mother and prayed no further grief would come.
units.literal: Looking up I served my loving mother, hoping for no later hardship.

units.zh: 凶災仍集，何辜於天。
units.en: Yet calamity returns—what sin have I committed against Heaven?
units.literal: Fierce disasters gather still—what crime against Heaven is this?

units.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
units.en: Alas for this sorrow!
units.literal: Alas, oh grief!

units.zh: 靈轜夙駕，設祖中闈。
units.en: At dawn the hearse stood ready; parting rites filled the inner court.
units.literal: The hearse was harnessed at dawn; farewell rites were set within the inner gate.

units.zh: 轀輬動軫，既往不追。
units.en: The jeweled hearse rolled forward—what is gone cannot be reclaimed.
units.literal: The burial wagon’s hubs rolled on—gone, never to pursue.

units.zh: 哀哀皇妣，永潛靈暉。
units.en: Royal mother most dear—your holy light is hid forever.
units.literal: Mournful royal mother—forever sunk beneath spiritual radiance.

units.zh: 進攀梓宮，顧援素旂。
units.en: I cling to your catalpa bier and clutch the mourning pennants as I climb.
units.literal: I advance to cling to the catalpa coffin, looking back to grasp the white banner.

units.zh: 屏營窮痛，誰告誰依？
units.en: I tremble with pain—whom can I tell, where find shelter?
units.literal: Trembling in utmost pain—whom shall I tell, on whom rely?

units.zh: 訴情贈策，以舒傷悲。
units.en: I pour my heart into this text to ease the ache that breaks me.
units.literal: I pour out feeling and present this document to ease wounded grief.

units.zh: 尚或有聞，顧予孤遺。
units.en: Perhaps you still may hear—turn once to your forsaken child.
units.literal: Perhaps you still may hear—look upon me, orphaned and left behind.

units.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
units.en: Alas for this sorrow!
units.literal: Alas, oh grief!

units.zh: 其後帝追慕不已，復下詔曰：「外曾祖母故司徒王朗夫人楊氏，舅氏尊屬，鄭、劉二從母，先后至愛。
units.en: Still grieving, he issued another edict: “Lady Yang, wife of former Minister Wang Lang and my maternal great-grandmother, together with my maternal uncles and my two aunts on the Zheng and Liu sides, were dearly loved by the late empress.
units.literal: Afterward the emperor’s longing did not cease; he again issued an edict saying: “My maternal great-grandmother, Lady Yang, wife of former Minister of Education Wang Lang, my uncles’ honored kin, and my two maternal aunts of the Zheng and Liu clans were deeply beloved by the late consorts.

units.zh: 每惟聖善，敦睦遺旨，渭陽之感，永懷靡及。
units.en: Whenever I recall their kindness and the generous instructions they left, the ache of a nephew for his mother’s kin stays with me yet can never be satisfied.
units.literal: Whenever pondering their sacred goodness and generous instructions, the Wei-yang longing—forever cherished yet never attained.

units.zh: 其封楊夫人及從母為鄉君，邑各五百戶。」
units.en: Let Lady Yang and my maternal aunts each receive the title of village mistress with five hundred taxable households.”
units.literal: Let Lady Yang and the maternal aunts be enfeoffed as village mistresses, five hundred households each.”

units.zh: 太康七年，追贈繼祖母夏侯氏為滎陽鄉君。
units.en: In 286 he posthumously named his step-grandmother Lady Xiahou village mistress of Xingyang.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Taikang, his step-grandmother Lady Xiahou was posthumously endowed as village mistress of Xingyang.

units.zh: 武元楊皇后
units.en: Empress Yang the Martial and Primordial
units.literal: Empress Yang Wuyuan

units.zh: 武元楊皇后諱艷，字瓊芝，弘農華陰人也。
units.en: Empress Yang Wuyuan, personal name Yan, courtesy Qiongzhi, came from Huayin in Hongnong commandery.
units.literal: Empress Yang Wuyuan, taboo name Yan, courtesy name Qiongzhi, was a native of Huayin in Hongnong.

units.zh: 父文宗，見《外戚傳》；
units.en: Her father Yang Wenzong [2] is treated in the “Treatise on Outer Kin”;
units.literal: Her father Wenzong [2]—see the “Treatise on Outer Kin”;

units.zh: 母天水趙氏，早卒。
units.en: her mother, a Zhao from Tianshui, died while Yang Yan was still young.
units.literal: her mother was a Zhao of Tianshui; she died early.

units.zh: 后依舅家，舅妻仁愛，親乳養后，遣他人乳其子。
units.en: She grew up in her uncle’s house; his wife nursed Yang Yan herself and hired another wet nurse for her own baby.
units.literal: The empress relied on her uncle’s household; her uncle’s wife was benevolent and loving, personally suckled and raised the empress, and sent another woman to nurse her own child.

units.zh: 及長，又隨後母段氏，依其家。
units.en: Later she lived under her stepmother Lady Duan’s roof.
units.literal: When grown, she again followed her stepmother Lady Duan and relied on that household.

units.zh: 后少聰慧，善書，姿質美麗，閑於女工。
units.en: From childhood she was bright and graceful, wrote well, was strikingly beautiful, and excelled at needlework.
units.literal: The empress was clever from youth, skilled at calligraphy, beautiful in bearing, and adept at women’s crafts.

units.zh: 有善相者嘗相后，當極貴，文帝聞而為世子聘焉。
units.en: A physiognomist predicted she would rise to the highest rank, and when Emperor Wen heard this he betrothed her to the crown prince.
units.literal: A skilled physiognomist once read the empress’s features and said she would reach supreme honor; Emperor Wen heard of it and betrothed her to the heir apparent.

units.zh: 甚被寵遇，生毗陵悼王軌、惠帝、秦獻王柬，平陽、新豐、陽平公主。
units.en: Deeply favored, she bore Prince Gui of Biling, Emperor Hui, Prince Jian of Qin, and the princesses of Pingyang, Xinfeng, and Yangping.
units.literal: She received great favor and bore Prince Gui of Biling, Emperor Hui, Prince Jian of Qin, and the princesses of Pingyang, Xinfeng, and Yangping.

units.zh: 武帝即位，立為皇后。
units.en: When Sima Yan became emperor, he made her empress.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he established her as empress.

units.zh: 有司奏依漢故事，皇后、太子各食湯沐邑四十縣，而帝以非古典，不許。
units.en: Officials asked that, as under Han custom, empress and heir each receive forty counties as bath-town fiefs, but the emperor refused as non-canonical.
units.literal: The offices memorialized that, following Han precedent, the empress and crown prince should each receive forty counties as bath-and-maintenance fiefs, but the emperor held this was not ancient practice and did not permit it.

units.zh: 后追懷舅氏之恩，顯官趙俊，納俊兄虞女粲於後宮為夫人。
units.en: Remembering her uncle’s kindness, she advanced Zhao Jun and took his brother’s daughter Zhao Can into the palace as Honored Lady.
units.literal: The empress recalled her debt to her mother’s clan, promoted Zhao Jun to high office, and brought Jun’s elder brother’s daughter Can into the inner palace as Honored Lady.

units.zh: 帝以皇太子不堪奉大統，密以語后。
units.en: Believing the crown prince unfit to inherit the realm, he confided as much privately to the empress.
units.literal: The emperor considered the crown prince unable to uphold the great line and secretly spoke of it to the empress.

units.zh: 后曰：「立嫡以長不以賢，豈可動乎？」
units.en: She replied, “The eldest legitimate son succeeds regardless of talent—how can we undo that?”
units.literal: The empress said: “Establishing the heir depends on seniority among legitimate sons, not on talent—how can that be altered?”

units.zh: 初，賈充妻郭氏使賂后，求以女為太子妃。
units.en: Earlier Jia Chong’s wife Lady Guo had bribed her to secure her daughter as crown princess.
units.literal: At first Jia Chong’s wife Lady Guo sent bribes to the empress, seeking to make her daughter crown princess.

units.zh: 及議太子婚，帝欲娶衛瓘女。
units.en: When the heir’s marriage came under debate, the emperor favored Wei Guan’s daughter.
units.literal: When discussing the crown prince’s marriage, the emperor wished to take Wei Guan’s daughter.

units.zh: 然后盛稱賈后有淑德，又密使太子太傅荀顗進言，上乃聽之。
units.en: The empress loudly praised Lady Jia’s virtue and secretly had Grand Tutor Xun Yi speak for her, so the emperor yielded.
units.literal: But the empress greatly praised Consort Jia’s virtuous conduct, and also secretly had Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince Xun Yi speak; the sovereign then consented.

units.zh: 泰始中，帝博選良家以充後宮，先下書禁天下嫁娶，使宦者乘使車，給騶騎，馳傳州郡，召充選者使后揀擇。
units.en: Midway through Taishi he cast a wide net for palace women, banned commoners from marrying, sent eunuchs in official carriages with escorts racing along post roads to every commandery, and had the candidates presented to the empress for her verdict.
units.literal: In the Taishi era the emperor broadly selected good families to fill the rear palace; first he issued a document forbidding marriage in the realm, had eunuchs ride dispatch coaches provided with outriders, gallop relay orders to provinces and commanderies, summon those filling selection and had the empress pick and choose.

units.zh: 后性妒，惟取潔白長大，其端正美麗者並不見留。
units.en: Jealous by nature, she kept only fair-skinned, tall girls and rejected every truly lovely face.
units.literal: The empress was by nature jealous; she only took those fair and tall; those properly beautiful were none of them retained.

units.zh: 時卞藩女有美色，帝掩扇謂后曰：「卞氏女佳。」
units.en: When Bian Fan’s daughter proved breathtaking, the emperor hid behind his fan and said, “The Bian girl is a jewel.”
units.literal: At the time Bian Fan’s daughter had beautiful looks; the emperor hid behind a fan and said to the empress: “Bian’s daughter is excellent.”

units.zh: 后曰：「藩三世后族，其女不可枉以卑位。」
units.en: The empress answered, “Three generations of Bians have supplied empresses—such a bride cannot be parked in a petty title.”
units.literal: The empress said: “The Bian clan for three generations has been empress kin—their daughter cannot be slighted with low rank.”

units.zh: 帝乃止。
units.en: He dropped the matter.
units.literal: The emperor then stopped.

units.zh: 司徒李胤、鎮軍大將軍胡奮、廷尉諸葛沖、太僕臧權、侍中馮蓀、秘書郎左思及世族子女並充三夫人九嬪之列。
units.en: The daughters of Li Yin, Hu Fen, Zhuge Chong, Zang Quan, Feng Sun, Zuo Si, and other great houses were placed among the Three Ladies and the Nine Concubines.
units.literal: Minister of Education Li Yin, General Who Guards the Army Hu Fen, Commandant of Justice Zhuge Chong, Grand Coachman Zang Quan, Palace Attendant Feng Sun, Secretary Court Gentleman Zuo Si, and daughters of eminent clans together filled the ranks of three ladies and nine bin.

units.zh: 司、冀、兗、豫四州二千石將吏家，補良人以下。
units.en: From Si, Ji, Yan, and Yu the daughters of prefects and local officers filled the ranks below Good Woman.
units.literal: Families of two-thousand-shi commandery officials in Si, Ji, Yan, and Yu four prefectures supplied ranks below liangren.

units.zh: 名家盛族子女，多敗衣瘁貌以避之。
units.en: Great families dressed their girls in rags and smeared their faces to dodge the draft.
units.literal: Sons and daughters of famous houses and great clans mostly wore tattered clothes and haggard looks to avoid it.

units.zh: 及后有疾，見帝素幸胡夫人，恐後立之，慮太子不安。
units.en: When she fell ill and saw how he favored Lady Hu, she feared a future empress would threaten her son.
units.literal: When the empress had illness, she saw the emperor always favored Lady Hu and feared she would later be established, worrying for the crown prince’s security.

units.zh: 臨終，枕帝膝曰：「叔父駿女男胤有德色，願陛下以備六宮。」
units.en: Dying with her head on his knee she said, “My uncle Yang Jun’s daughter Nanyin combines virtue and beauty—please bring her into the six palaces.”
units.literal: At the end, pillowing on the emperor’s knee she said: “My uncle Yang Jun’s daughter Nanyin has virtue and beauty; I beg Your Majesty to keep her for the six palaces.”

units.zh: 因悲泣，帝流涕許之。
units.en: She wept; he swore through tears to comply.
units.literal: Thereupon she wept sadly; the emperor promised with flowing tears.

units.zh: 泰始十年，崩於明光殿，絕于帝膝，時年三十七。
units.en: She died in 274 in Mingguang Hall on his lap, thirty-seven years old.
units.literal: In the tenth Taishi year she died in Mingguang Hall, expired on the emperor’s knee, aged thirty-seven.

units.zh: 詔曰：「皇后逮事先后，常冀能終始永奉宗廟，一旦殂隕，痛悼傷懷。
units.en: The edict read, “The empress served my late mothers and hoped to honor the shrines to the end; her sudden death tears my heart.
units.literal: An edict said: “The empress served the late consorts in succession, always hoping to be able from beginning to end forever to serve the ancestral temple; suddenly she has fallen—pain and grief wound the heart.

units.zh: 每自以夙喪二親，於家門之情特隆。
units.en: Orphaned young, she cherished family ties above all else.
units.literal: She often because early lost both parents, toward household affection was especially strong.

units.zh: 又有心欲改葬父祖，以頃者務崇儉約，初不有言，近垂困，說此意，情亦愍之。
units.en: She longed to rebury her father and grandfather but, while court fashion prized austerity, stayed silent until her final hours—this wish moves us still.
units.literal: Also she had in mind wishing to rebury her father and grandfather; because recent affairs strove to esteem thrift, at first she did not speak; drawing near to death’s agony she stated this intent—the feeling also pities her.

units.zh: 其使領前軍將軍駿等自克改葬之宜，至時，主者供給葬事。
units.en: Let Forward-General Yang Jun and his colleagues arrange the reburials; officials shall supply whatever is needed when the day comes.
units.literal: Let General of the Van Yang Jun and others themselves determine the propriety of reburial; when the time comes, those in charge shall supply burial affairs.

units.zh: 賜諡母趙氏為縣君，以繼母段氏為鄉君。
units.en: Honor her mother Lady Zhao as county mistress and her stepmother Lady Duan as village mistress.
units.literal: Posthumously grant Lady Zhao mother title as county mistress, and stepmother Lady Duan as village mistress.

units.zh: 傳不云乎，『慎終追遠，民德歸厚』。
units.en: Has not the classic said, ‘Care for the dead and honor the past, and the people grow in virtue’?
units.literal: Does not the tradition say, ‘Being careful in one’s end and remembering the remote makes the people’s virtue thick’?

units.zh: 且使亡者有知，尚或嘉之。」
units.en: Should the dead still know anything of us, they may rejoice in this kindness.”
units.literal: Moreover, if the dead have knowledge, perhaps they will approve.”

units.zh: 于是有司卜吉，窀穸有期，乃命史臣作哀策敘懷。
units.en: Officers chose an auspicious day for interment and scribes were told to write a lament.
units.literal: Thereupon the officials divined an auspicious day; the burial had a set time; then he ordered the scribes to compose a dirge narrating feeling.

units.zh: 其詞曰：
units.en: It reads:
units.literal: The words say:

units.zh: 天地配序，成化兩儀。
units.en: Heaven and earth keep their stations and shape the yin and yang spheres.
units.literal: Heaven and earth match in sequence; they accomplish transformation of the two modes.

units.zh: 王假有家，道在伉儷。
units.en: The king wins a true household because husband and wife uphold the Way.
units.literal: The king comes to have a household; the way lies in husband and wife.

units.zh: 姜嫄佐嚳，二妃興媯。
units.en: Jiang Yuan aided Emperor Ku; the two brides raised the house of Gui.
units.literal: Jiang Yuan aided Ku; two consorts raised Gui.

units.zh: 仰希古昔，冀亦同規。
units.en: We look to antiquity and pray our norm matches theirs.
units.literal: Looking up I hope in ancient past; I hope likewise same norm.

units.zh: 今胡不然，景命夙虧。
units.en: Why are we denied that grace—why was her bright mandate cut short?
units.literal: Now why is it not so—the bright mandate early deficient?

units.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
units.en: Alas for this sorrow!
units.literal: Alas, oh grief!

units.zh: 我應圖籙，統臨萬方。
units.en: I hold the celestial charts and rule the myriad lands.
units.literal: I respond to charts and tallies, overseeing the myriad regions.

units.zh: 正位于內，實在嬪嬙。
units.en: The inner court’s order rests with its ladies.
units.literal: Correct position lies within; truly it lies in the consorts.

units.zh: 天作之合，駿發之祥。
units.en: Heaven forged our match and sent forth splendid omens.
units.literal: Heaven made the match; splendidly arose auspice.

units.zh: 河嶽降靈，啟祚華陽。
units.en: River and peak lent her spirit and opened blessing in Huayang.
units.literal: Rivers and peaks sent down spirits; they opened fortune at Huayang.

units.zh: 奕世豐衍，朱紼斯煌。
units.en: Generation on generation flourished; vermillion seals blaze forth.
units.literal: Generation after generation abundant spread; vermillion cords thus shine.

units.zh: 纘女惟行，受命溥將。
units.en: She renewed womanly duty and answered Heaven’s wide charge.
units.literal: Continue the woman’s conduct; receive mandate broadly to assist.

units.zh: 來翼家邦，憲度是常。
units.en: She came to shield house and realm and held fast to every norm.
units.literal: Come to wing the state and house; statute and measure are the constant.

units.zh: 緝熙陰教，德聲顯揚。
units.en: She brightened women’s teaching and her fair fame rang wide.
units.literal: Brighten women’s instruction; virtue’s fame is displayed.

units.zh: 昔我先妣，暉曜休光。
units.en: My late mother shone with auspicious light.
units.literal: Formerly my late mother—brilliant glorious auspicious light.

units.zh: 后承前訓，奉述遺芳。
units.en: This empress followed her teaching and kept her fragrance alive.
units.literal: The empress received former instruction; she upheld and narrated remaining fragrance.

units.zh: 宜嗣徽音，繼序無荒。
units.en: She should have prolonged that sweet renown and kept our line from wandering astray.
units.literal: Should continue fine reputation; continue the sequence without waste.

units.zh: 如何不弔，背世隕喪。
units.en: Why should Heaven not pity her—she left the living world too soon.
units.literal: How can we not mourn—she turned her back on the age and collapsed.

units.zh: 望齊無主，長去烝嘗。
units.en: Ancestral feasts in Qi lack their host; steam offerings rise without her.
units.literal: Gazing toward Qi she has no lord; forever gone are winter and summer sacrifices.

units.zh: 追懷永悼，率土摧傷。
units.en: Memory cuts deep; the whole realm shares this wound.
units.literal: Tracing remembrance brings endless mourning; across the soil every heart breaks.

units.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
units.en: Alas for this sorrow!
units.literal: Alas, oh grief!

units.zh: 陵兆既窆，將遷幽都。
units.en: The vault is closed; her shades depart for darkness.
units.literal: The tumulus ground already narrowed; she will move to the silent capital.

units.zh: 宵陳夙駕，元妃其徂。
units.en: Torches at midnight, dawn departure—the queen sets forth.
units.literal: At midnight they harness at dawn; the chief consort journeys hence.

units.zh: 宮闈遏密，階庭空虛。
units.en: The inner halls fall silent; courtyard stairs lie bare.
units.literal: The palace gates fall mute; steps and courts stand empty.

units.zh: 設祖布紼，告駕啟塗。
units.en: Bearers array cords of parting, proclaim the hearse, and clear the way.
units.literal: They set the farewell rites, spread the mourning sash, announce the coach and open the road.

units.zh: 服翬褕狄，寄象容車。
units.en: Kingfisher seams and pheasant gown ride with her image on the draped bier.
units.literal: She wears kingfisher robe and barren-rabbit cloak; her likeness rides the draped coach.

units.zh: 金路晻藹，裳帳不舒。
units.en: Gold carriage lamps flicker; pall curtains stay furled in grief.
units.literal: The golden carriage dimly veils; skirts and curtains do not spread.

units.zh: 千乘動軫，六驥躊躇。
units.en: Countless wheels roll; six bays champ at their traces.
units.literal: A thousand carriages stir their hubs; six chestnuts paw and linger.

units.zh: 銘旌樹表，翣柳雲敷。
units.en: Spirit pennons lift high; plumed shades drift like clouds.
units.literal: The inscribed banner marks the way; feather screens sweep cloud-like.

units.zh: 祁祁同軌，岌岌烝徒。
units.en: All realms march together; the funeral train towers sheer.
units.literal: So many share one road; awed mourners throng on foot.

units.zh: 孰不云懷，哀感萬夫。
units.en: Who could withhold tears—a myriad souls ache together.
units.literal: Who fails to cherish her—ten thousand hearts ache at once.

units.zh: 寧神虞卜，安體玄廬。
units.en: Give her peace per oracle rites; settle her in the earthen vault.
units.literal: Calm her spirit with Yu’s divination; lay her body to rest in the dark lodge.

units.zh: 土房陶簋，齊制遂初。
units.en: Clay chamber and pottery jars restore the humble pattern from her youth.
units.literal: Earthen chamber and pottery vessels match the plain rules of her first estate.

units.zh: 依行紀諡，聲被八區。
units.en: Virtue frames her epithet; her name crosses every quarter.
units.literal: Align deed with posthumous title; her fame reaches all eight quarters.

units.zh: 雖背明光，亦歸皇姑。
units.en: Though she leaves the sunny halls, she rests beside her queenly ancestress.
units.literal: Though she leaves Mingguang’s light, she joins her royal mother-in-law.

units.zh: 沒而不朽，世德作謨。
units.en: Death cannot dissolve her—her house’s virtue turns scripture.
units.literal: She sinks yet does not decay—worldly virtue becomes model for ages.

units.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
units.en: Alas for this sorrow!
units.literal: Alas, oh grief!

units.zh: 乃葬于峻陽陵。
units.en: They laid her to rest at Junyang.
units.literal: She was buried at Junyang Mausoleum.

units.zh: 武悼楊皇后
units.en: Empress Yang the Martial and Mourned
units.literal: Empress Yang Wudao

units.zh: 武悼楊皇后諱芷，字季蘭，小字男胤，元后從妹。
units.en: Empress Yang Wudao—personal name Zhi, courtesy Jilan, pet name Nanyin—was cousin to the founding empress.
units.literal: Empress Yang Wudao, taboo name Zhi, courtesy name Jilan, childhood name Nanyin, was a younger cousin of Empress Yuan.

units.zh: 父駿，別有傳。
units.en: Her father Yang Jun has his own biography.
units.literal: Her father Jun has a separate biography.

units.zh: 以咸寧二年立為皇后。
units.en: She became empress in 276.
units.literal: In the second Xianning year she was established as empress.

units.zh: 婉嫕有婦德，美映椒房，甚有寵。
units.en: Gentle and virtuous, she brightened the harem and won enduring favor.
units.literal: Gracious and yielding, she possessed womanly virtue; her beauty lit the pepper chambers and she enjoyed deep favor.

units.zh: 生渤海殤王，早薨，遂無子。
units.en: Her son the prince of Bohai died in infancy, leaving her without heirs.
units.literal: She bore Prince Huaihai of Bohai, who died young; thereafter she had no sons.

units.zh: 太康九年，后率內外夫人命婦躬桑于西郊，賜帛各有差。
units.en: In 288 she led court ladies to the western suburban silkworm rite and dispensed silk rewards by rank.
units.literal: In the ninth Taikang year the empress led palace ladies and titled wives to tend silkworms at the western suburb and granted silk in graded amounts.

units.zh: 太子妃賈氏妒忌，帝將廢之。
units.en: Jealous Crown Princess Jia faced deposition.
units.literal: Crown Princess Jia was jealous; the emperor was about to depose her.

units.zh: 后言於帝曰：「賈公閭有勳社稷，猶當數世宥之。
units.en: She urged him, “Jia Chong secured the dynasty—his clan merits lasting grace.
units.literal: The empress said to the emperor: “Lord Jia has merit for state—his house deserves indulgence for generations.

units.zh: 賈妃親是其女，正復妒忌之間，不足以一眚掩其大德。」
units.en: His daughter is princess—in mere spite one flaw cannot bury his great merit."
units.literal: The Jia consort is his own daughter; amid jealousy alone, one blemish cannot veil his great virtue.”

units.zh: 后又數誡厲妃，妃不知后之助己，因以致恨，謂后構之於帝，忿怨彌深。
units.en: She later scolded the princess repeatedly; blind to this help, Jia Nanfeng blamed her for slander and hated her all the more.
units.literal: Later she repeatedly warned and rebuked the princess; the princess did not realize the empress aided her and therefore bore hatred, believing the empress framed her before the emperor—resentment grew deeper.

units.zh: 及帝崩，尊為皇太后。
units.en: After Emperor Wu died she became empress dowager.
units.literal: When the emperor died, she was honored as empress dowager.

units.zh: 賈后凶悖，忌后父駿執權，遂誣駿為亂，使楚王瑋與東安王繇稱詔誅駿。
units.en: Vicious Jia Nanfeng feared Yang Jun; she accused him of treason and had Sima Wei and Sima Yao murder him with forged orders.
units.literal: Empress Jia was vicious; she resented her father Jun holding power, then slandered Jun as rebellious and had Prince Chu Wei and Prince Dongan Yao forge edicts to execute Jun.

units.zh: 內外隔塞，后題帛為書，射之城外，曰「救太傅者有賞」，賈后因宣言太后同逆。
units.en: Cut off from aid, she shot silk pleas over the wall saying, "Whoever rescues the Grand Tutor will be rewarded"; Jia then claimed the dowager joined the plot.
units.literal: Inner and outer courts were blocked; the empress wrote on silk, shot it beyond the walls, saying “Whoever rescues the grand tutor will be rewarded”; Empress Jia then declared the dowager abetted treason.

units.zh: 駿既死，詔使後軍將軍荀悝送后于永寧宮。
units.en: After Yang Jun fell, Rear-General Xun Kui was ordered to move her to Yongning Palace.
units.literal: After Jun died, an edict ordered Rear-General Xun Kui to escort the empress to Yongning Palace.

units.zh: 特全后母高都君龐氏之命，聽就后居止。
units.en: Her mother Lady Pang was spared and permitted to live with her.
units.literal: Her mother Lady Pang of Gaodu Commandery was specially spared and allowed to stay with the dowager.

units.zh: 賈后諷群公有司奏曰：「皇太后陰漸姦謀，圖危社稷，飛箭繫書，要募將士，同惡相濟，自絕于天。
units.en: Jia’s faction petitioned: “The dowager schemed treason, imperiled the state, shot letters beyond the walls, and recruited troops—criminals helped her and Heaven abandoned her.
units.literal: Empress Jia prompted assembled dukes and offices to memorialize: “The empress dowager secretly carried treason, plotted against the altars, flew arrows with letters tied, summoned soldiers—wicked men aided her and she cut herself off from Heaven.

units.zh: 魯侯絕文姜，春秋所許，蓋以奉順祖宗，任至公於天下。
units.en: Lu cut ties with Wen Jiang, which the Annals condone, to serve ancestors and justice.
units.literal: Duke Lu cut off Wen Jiang—the Spring and Autumn approves—because one must honor ancestors and hold utmost fairness toward the realm.

units.zh: 陛下雖懷無已之情，臣下不敢奉詔。
units.en: We know your grief, sire, yet we cannot sanction mercy.
units.literal: Although Your Majesty harbors endless feeling, your servants dare not obey the edict.

units.zh: 可宣敕王公于朝堂會議。」
units.en: Summon princes and ministers to the outer court for debate.”
units.literal: Let an order proclaim that kings and dukes convene in the court hall to deliberate.”

units.zh: 詔曰：「此大事，更詳之。」
units.en: The throne replied, “Weighty—deliberate further.”
units.literal: An edict said: “This is a great matter—consider it again.”

units.zh: 有司又奏：「駿藉外戚之資，居冢宰之任，陛下既居諒闇，委以重權，至乃陰圖凶逆，布樹私黨。
units.en: They answered: “Yang Jun used kinship to seize power; while you mourned he plotted rebellion and packed offices with clients.
units.literal: The offices again memorialized: “Jun relied on affinal backing and held prime minister’s charge; while Your Majesty mourned in the dark palace he received heavy trust, yet secretly plotted treason and planted private partisans.

units.zh: 皇太后內為脣齒，協同逆謀，禍釁既彰，背捍詔命，阻兵負眾，血刃宮省，而復流書募眾，以獎凶黨，上背祖宗之靈，下絕億兆之望。
units.en: The dowager abetted him; when crime surfaced she resisted orders, armed her faction, and stained the palace—yet still shot appeals to arm traitors, dishonoring spirits and people.
units.literal: The empress dowager was his lip and tooth within; she joined the wicked plot. Once the stench showed, she defied decrees, blocked armies, and bloodied the palace—yet still flew letters to recruit crowds and reward villains, betraying ancestors above and cutting off the myriad hopes below.

units.zh: 昔文姜與亂，春秋所貶，呂宗叛戾，高后降配，宜廢皇太后為峻陽庶人。」
units.en: Like Wen Jiang or Empress Lü, she must be struck from dowager rank and made a commoner of Junyang.”
units.literal: Formerly Wen Jiang joined turmoil—the Spring and Autumn demoted her; the Lü clan rebelled and Empress Gao was lowered in pairing. She should be demoted from empress dowager to commoner of Junyang.”

units.zh: 中書監張華等以為「太后非得罪于先帝者也，今黨惡所親，[3]為不母于聖世。
units.en: Zhang Hua argued: “She never wronged Emperor Wu; siding with villains now breaks maternal duty in our era [3].
units.literal: Palace Supervisor Zhang Hua and others held: “The dowager did not offend the late emperor; now she joins wicked kin—she fails motherhood toward this sage age [3].

units.zh: 宜依孝成趙皇后故事，曰武帝皇后，處之離宮，以全貴終之恩。」
units.en: Treat her like Chengdi’s Zhao—call her Emperor Wu’s consort, lodge her apart, yet grant a decent end.”
units.literal: She should follow Empress Zhao of Emperor Cheng’s precedent—styled Empress of Emperor Wu and housed in a detached palace to preserve honored kindness to the end.”

units.zh: 尚書令、下邳王晃等議曰：「皇太后與駿潛謀，欲危社稷，不可復奉承宗廟，配合先帝。
units.en: Sima Huang, Prince of Xiapi and Director of the Department of State Affairs, countered: “She conspired with Yang Jun—she cannot share Wu’s temple.
units.literal: The Director of the Department of State Affairs, Sima Huang, Prince of Xiapi, and others debated: “The empress dowager secretly plotted with Jun to overturn the state—she cannot again serve the temple or pair with the late emperor.

units.zh: 宜貶尊號，廢詣金墉城。」
units.en: Strip her titles and lock her in Jinyong.”
units.literal: Her honored title should be stripped and she banished to Metal-Walled Fortress.”

units.zh: 于是有司奏：「請從晃等議，廢太后為庶人。
units.en: Officials petitioned: "We ask to adopt Huang's proposal and depose the dowager as a commoner.
units.literal: Thereupon the offices petitioned: “We ask following Huang’s proposal—depose the dowager as commoner.

units.zh: 遣使者以太牢告于郊廟，以奉承祖宗之命，稱萬國之望。
units.en: Announce it with suburban bull sacrifice to ancestors and satisfy the realm.
units.literal: Dispatch envoys with grand sacrifice to announce at suburban altars and ancestral temple, obeying ancestor spirits and answering myriad lands’ expectation.

units.zh: 至於諸所供奉，可順聖恩，務從豐厚。」
units.en: Let her maintenance stay generous per your mercy.”
units.literal: As for all provisions supplied, follow sagely kindness and strive for abundance.”

units.zh: 詔不許。
units.en: The emperor refused.
units.literal: The edict did not permit.

units.zh: 有司又固請，乃可之。
units.en: They insisted again; he yielded.
units.literal: The offices pressed again; then he consented.

units.zh: 又奏：「楊駿造亂，家屬應誅，詔原其妻龐命，以慰太后之心。
units.en: They added: “Yang Jun’s clan should die; you spared Lady Pang to comfort the dowager.
units.literal: They also memorialized: “Yang Jun raised rebellion—his kin deserve execution; the edict spared his wife Pang to console the dowager.

units.zh: 今太后廢為庶人，請以龐付廷尉行刑。」
units.en: Now that she is a commoner, execute Lady Pang.”
units.literal: Now that the dowager is demoted to commoner, we ask that Pang be handed to the Commandant of Justice for execution.”

units.zh: 詔曰：「聽龐與庶人相隨。」
units.en: He ruled: “Let Lady Pang stay with her.”
units.literal: The edict said: “Let Pang follow the commoner.”

units.zh: 有司希賈后旨，固請，乃從之。
units.en: Bowing to Jia’s will they insisted until he agreed.
units.literal: The offices, courting Empress Jia’s intent, pressed firmly; then he followed.

units.zh: 龐臨刑，太后抱持號叫，截髮稽顙，上表詣賈后稱妾，請全母命，不見省。
units.en: At Lady Pang’s execution the dowager clung to her, cut her hair, kowtowed, signed herself Jia’s servant to beg for mercy—Jia ignored her.
units.literal: When Pang faced execution, the empress dowager clutched her, wailing; she cut her hair and knocked her forehead, submitted a memorial as concubine to Empress Jia begging to save her mother’s life—she was not granted audience.

units.zh: 初，太后尚有侍御十餘人，賈后奪之，絕膳而崩，時年三十四，在位十五年。
units.en: Jia stripped her servants; she starved at thirty-four after fifteen years as consort.
units.literal: At first the dowager still had more than ten attendants; Empress Jia seized them; she starved and died, aged thirty-four, having held rank fifteen years.

units.zh: 賈后又信妖巫，謂太后必訴冤先帝，乃覆而殯之，施諸厭劾符書藥物。
units.en: Jia feared her ghost would accuse Emperor Wu, so she buried her prone under talismans.
units.literal: Empress Jia further trusted witchcraft, fearing the dowager would appeal her grievance to the late emperor; she therefore buried her face-down with curse charms and drugs.

units.zh: 永嘉元年，追復尊號，別立廟，神主不配武帝。
units.en: In 307 her title was restored, a separate shrine was built, and her tablet was not enshrined with Emperor Wu.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongjia her honored title was restored, a separate temple was established, and her spirit tablet was not paired with Emperor Wu.

units.zh: 至成帝咸康七年，下詔使內外詳議。
units.en: In 341 Emperor Cheng ordered court and capital officials to deliberate the question fully.
units.literal: By the seventh year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng, an edict ordered inner and outer officials to debate the matter in detail.

units.zh: 衛將軍虞潭議曰：世祖武皇帝光有四海，元皇后應乾作配。
units.en: Guards General Yu Tan argued: “Emperor Wu illumined the realm; his first empress answered Heaven.”
units.literal: Guards General Yu Tan argued: “Shizu Emperor Wu glorified the four seas; his primal empress matched Heaven’s pivot.”

units.zh: 元后既崩，悼后繼作，至楊駿肆逆，禍延天母。
units.en: After Yang Yan died came Yang Zhi; Yang Jun’s treason dragged down the queen mother.
units.literal: After the primal empress died, the mourned empress succeeded; when Yang Jun ran riot, calamity reached the Mother of Heaven.

units.zh: 孝懷皇帝追復號諡，豈不以鯀殛禹興，義在不替者乎！
units.en: Huai restored her honors—as Gun fell but Yu rose, duty survives.
units.literal: Emperor Huai restored her title and epithet—is this not because Gun was executed yet Yu rose—the principle of unbroken obligation?

units.zh: 又太寧二年，臣忝宗正，帝譜泯棄，罔所循按。
units.en: In the second year of Taining I held the clan office; registers were gone.
units.literal: Moreover in the second Taining year I humbly served as Director of the Imperial Clan; imperial genealogies were lost—nothing to consult.

units.zh: 時博諮舊齒，以定昭穆，與故驃騎將軍華恒、尚書荀崧、侍中荀邃因舊譜參論撰次，尊號之重，一無改替。
units.en: With Hua Heng, Xun Song, and Xun Sui we recomposed charts—her rank stood firm.
units.literal: We broadly queried elders to fix generations and, with former General of Agile Cavalry Hua Heng, Minister Xun Song, Palace Attendant Xun Sui, reviewed old lists to compile order—her lofty title stayed unchanged.

units.zh: 今聖上孝思，祗肅禋祀，詢及群司，將以恢定大禮。
units.en: Today’s ruler seeks your counsel to fix court ritual.
units.literal: Now our sage sovereign’s filial care solemnly tends sacrifice; he asks all bureaus to settle great ritual.

units.zh: 臣輒思詳，伏見惠皇帝起居注、群臣議奏，列駿作逆謀，危社稷，引魯之文姜，漢之呂后。
units.en: Hui’s archives cite Wen Jiang and Empress Lü against Yang Jun.
units.literal: I have reflected carefully: in Emperor Hui’s daily records and ministers’ memorials they listed Jun’s treason, imperiling altars, citing Lu’s Wen Jiang and Han’s Empress Lü.

units.zh: 臣竊以文姜雖莊公之母，實為父讎；
units.en: Wen Jiang was Duke Huan’s killer despite bearing Zhuang—
units.literal: I quietly note that although Wen Jiang was Duke Zhuang’s mother, she was truly her husband’s foe;

units.zh: 呂后寵樹私戚，幾危劉氏，按此二事異于今日。
units.en: Empress Lü nearly ruined Han—these differ from Yang Zhi.
units.literal: Empress Lü favored kin until she nearly ended the Liu house—these two cases differ from today.

units.zh: 昔漢章帝竇后殺和帝之母，和帝即位盡誅諸竇。
units.en: Zhangdi’s Dou killed He’s mother; He wiped out the Dous.
units.literal: Formerly Dou empress of Han Zhangdi killed Emperor He’s mother; when He ascended he slaughtered the Dou clan.

units.zh: 當時議者欲貶竇后，及后之亡，欲不以禮葬。
units.en: Critics then sought to shame Dou and withhold burial rites.
units.literal: Debates then wished to demote Dou empress; when she died some wished denial of ritual burial.

units.zh: 和帝以奉事十年，義不可違，臣子之道，務從豐厚，仁明之稱，表于往代。
units.en: He refused cruelty after ten years’ care—his mercy became legend.
units.literal: He had served her ten years—duty forbade cruelty; ministers pursued lavish burial—his humanity shone for ages.

units.zh: 又見故尚書僕射裴頠議悼后故事，稱繼母雖出，追服無改。
units.en: The late Vice Director Pei Wei, discussing the precedent of the Mourned Empress, held that mourning for a stepmother continues even after she is cast out.
units.literal: I also saw the late Vice Director Pei Wei’s opinion on the Mourned Empress’s case—though a stepmother had been cast out, mourning obligations stayed unchanged.

units.zh: 是以孝懷皇帝尊崇號諡，還葬峻陵。
units.en: So Huai restored her posthumous honors at Junling.
units.literal: Therefore Emperor Huai restored honored title and epithet and reburied her at Jun Mausoleum.

units.zh: 此則母子道全，而廢事蕩革也。
units.en: Kin duty survived though politics had fouled them.
units.literal: Thus mother-son duty stayed whole while violent deeds were swept away.

units.zh: 于時祭于弘訓之宮，未入太廟。
units.en: She received offerings only at Hongxun, not the grand temple.
units.literal: At that time sacrifice occurred at Hongxun Palace—not yet entering the great temple.

units.zh: 蓋是事之未盡，非義典也。
units.en: That showed work unfinished, not proper liturgy.
units.literal: That was because the matter was unfinished—not canonical meaning.

units.zh: 若以悼后復位為宜，則應配食世祖；
units.en: If Yang Zhi deserves restoration, she must join Wu’s temple;
units.literal: If restoring Empress Dao is right, she should share Emperor Wu’s offerings;

units.zh: 若以復之為非，則譜諡宜闕，未有位號居正，而偏祠別室者也。
units.en: if not, her titles should lapse—no legitimate rank receives only a side altar.
units.literal: if restoring her is wrong, then genealogies and epithets should lapse—one cannot hold orthodox rank yet dwell in a side shrine alone.

units.zh: 若以孝懷皇帝私隆母子之道，特為立廟者，此苟崇私情，有虧國典，則國譜帝諱，皆宜除棄，匪徒不得同祀于世祖之廟也。
units.en: A private shrine for filial piety alone would break precedent and void every register.
units.literal: If Emperor Huai privately enlarged mother-son feeling and built a special temple, that would exalt private affection yet wound state canon—then clan registers and temple names should all be discarded, not merely barred from Wu’s temple.

units.zh: 會稽王昱、中書監庾冰、中書令何充、尚書令諸葛恢、尚書謝廣、光祿勳留擢、丹楊尹殷融、護軍將軍馮懷、散騎常侍鄧逸等咸從潭議，由是太后配食武帝。
units.en: Sima Yu, Prince of Kuaiji, Yu Bing, He Chong, Zhuge Hui, Xie Guang, Liu Zhuo, Yin Rong, Feng Huai, and Deng Yi endorsed Tan—Yang Zhi joined Wu’s temple.
units.literal: Sima Yu, Prince of Kuaiji, Palace Supervisor Yu Bing, Palace Director He Chong, Minister Director Zhuge Hui, Minister Xie Guang, Superintendent of the Household Liu Zhuo, Intendant of Danyang Yin Rong, Defender-general Feng Huai, and Palace Rider Deng Yi all followed Tan’s opinion; thereby the dowager shared Emperor Wu’s sacrifices.

units.zh: 左貴嬪
units.en: Lady Zuo of Honorable Rank
units.literal: Honorable Lady Zuo

units.zh: 左貴嬪名芬。
units.en: Lady Zuo Fen bore that name.
units.literal: The honorable lady Zuo was named Fen.

units.zh: 兄思，別有傳。
units.en: Her brother Zuo Si has his own biography.
units.literal: Her brother Si has a separate biography.

units.zh: 芬少好學，善綴文，名亞于思，武帝聞而納之。
units.en: A scholar and poet second only to Zuo Si, she entered Emperor Wu’s harem by reputation.
units.literal: Fen from youth loved learning, excelled at composing, her fame second only to Si’s; Emperor Wu heard of her and took her in.

units.zh: 泰始八年，拜修儀。
units.en: In 272 she became Xiuyi.
units.literal: In the eighth Taishi year she was appointed Xiuyi.

units.zh: 受詔作愁思之文，因為離思賦曰：
units.en: Ordered to write on longing, she penned “Rhapsody on Parting Longing”:
units.literal: Receiving an edict to compose a text on sorrowful longing, she therefore wrote the “Rhapsody on Parting Longing,” saying:

units.zh: 生蓬戶之側陋兮，不閑習於文符。
units.en: Raised by a humble gate—I never studied formal genres.
units.literal: Born beside a ramshackle gate—I never practiced literary tokens.

units.zh: 不見圖畫之妙像兮，不聞先哲之典謨。
units.en: I never traced gallery portraits nor heard wise exempla.
units.literal: I never saw painted beauties nor heard ancient sages’ counsels.

units.zh: 既愚陋而寡識兮，謬忝廁于紫廬。
units.en: Crude and shallow, I stumbled into the purple halls.
units.literal: Dull and ignorant, yet wrongly admitted to the purple lodge.

units.zh: 非草苗之所處兮，恒怵惕以憂懼。
units.en: I am grass out of place—I live in constant fear.
units.literal: No weed seedling belongs here—I tremble ever in dread.

units.zh: 懷思慕之忉怛兮，兼始終之萬慮。
units.en: Love and sorrow knot every moment.
units.literal: Cherishing longing’s ache, I bear myriad cares from first to last.

units.zh: 嗟隱憂之沈積兮，獨鬱結而靡訴。
units.en: Hidden grief heaps high; I choke with words unsaid.
units.literal: Alas, hidden grief piles deep—alone I knot inward with nowhere to speak.

units.zh: 意慘憒而無聊兮，思纏綿以增慕。
units.en: My spirit dulls; longing coils tighter.
units.literal: My heart is bleak and restless; longing winds tighter and deepens love.

units.zh: 夜耿耿而不寐兮，魂憧憧而至曙。
units.en: Nights are endless; my soul drifts till daylight.
units.literal: Night stretches sleepless; my soul wanders until dawn.

units.zh: 風騷騷而四起兮，霜皚皚而依庭。
units.en: Wind sighs on four sides; frost lines the yard.
units.literal: Wind whistles from every side; frost gleams white along the courtyard.

units.zh: 日晻曖而無光兮，氣懰慄以洌清。
units.en: Sunlight fades; the air cuts cold.
units.literal: The sun dims without light; the air bites sharp and clear.

units.zh: 懷愁戚之多感兮，患涕淚之自零。
units.en: Sorrow crowds my breast; tears fall unbidden.
units.literal: Breast laden with sorrow’s many blows—I fear tears falling of themselves.

units.zh: 昔伯瑜之婉孌兮，每綵衣以娛親。
units.en: Long ago Boyu, in tender devotion, wore bright robes to delight his kin.
units.literal: Ancient Boyu was tender—he often donned colored robes to cheer his parents.

units.zh: 悼今日之乖隔兮，奄與家為參辰。
units.en: Today’s cruel divide casts kin as stars that never meet.
units.literal: I mourn today’s cruel separation—suddenly with family I am Orion and Sirius.

units.zh: 豈相去之云遠兮，曾不盈乎數尋。
units.en: We stand mere feet apart yet cannot bridge the gap.
units.literal: How can they say the distance is far—it does not fill a few yards’ span.

units.zh: 何宮禁之清切兮，欲瞻睹而莫因。
units.en: Palace gates cut sharply—no path opens for my gaze.
units.literal: How sternly clear are palace barriers—I long to gaze yet find no way.

units.zh: 仰行雲以歔欷兮，涕流射而沾巾。
units.en: I gaze at clouds and weep; tears stream until my sleeves drip.
units.literal: I lift my eyes to drifting clouds and sigh; tears jet forth soaking my kerchief.

units.zh: 惟屈原之哀感兮，嗟悲傷于離別。
units.en: Qu Yuan knew this ache—parting tears fall anew.
units.literal: Only Qu Yuan’s sorrow moves—alas for parting’s grief.

units.zh: 彼城闕之作詩兮，亦以日而喻月。
units.en: The poets at the gate tower likened sun and moon—
units.literal: Those who made poems at the gate tower likewise paired sun with moon.

units.zh: 況骨肉之相於兮，永緬邈而兩絕。
units.en: —yet kinship binds tighter than sun and moon, now lost forever.
units.literal: How much more flesh and bone sharing breath—forever distant, severed both ways.

units.zh: 長含哀而抱戚兮，仰蒼天而泣血。
units.en: Endless sorrow grips me; I lift my eyes to Heaven and weep blood.
units.literal: Long bearing sorrow with clasped grief—I lift blue Heaven and weep blood.

units.zh: 亂曰：骨肉至親，化為他人，永長辭兮。
units.en: Envoi: closest kin turned stranger—gone forever.
units.literal: Envoi: flesh and bone most dear become strangers—forever gone.

units.zh: 慘愴愁悲，夢想魂歸，見所思兮。
units.en: Bitter grief—dreaming souls return with remembered faces.
units.literal: Anguish and drear longing—dreaming souls return to show those missed.

units.zh: 驚寤號咷，心不自聊，泣漣洏兮。
units.en: Waking with a cry the heart finds no rest; tears thread endlessly.
units.literal: Startled awake I wail—the heart finds no ease; tears trickle down.

units.zh: 援筆舒情，涕淚增零，訴斯詩兮。
units.en: Brush in hand I bare grief; tears fall faster as I write these lines.
units.literal: I take brush to vent feeling—tears multiply as I speak this poem.

units.zh: 後為貴嬪，姿陋無寵，以才德見禮。
units.en: Raised to honorable lady despite plain looks, she won respect through wit and character.
units.literal: Later she became honorable lady—plain in looks without favor, honored for talent and virtue.

units.zh: 體羸多患，常居薄室，帝每遊華林，輒回輦過之。
units.en: Frail and sickly, she kept to spare rooms; each imperial outing to Splendid Grove detoured past her lodge.
units.literal: Her frame frail and often ill, she dwelt in modest chambers; whenever the emperor toured Splendid Grove he turned his carriage to pass her gate.

units.zh: 言及文義，辭對清華，左右侍聽，莫不稱美。
units.en: Her answers on texts sparkled; every listener praised her grace.
units.literal: When discourse touched literary meaning her replies were lucid and splendid; attendants left and right listened—none failed to praise.

units.zh: 及元楊皇后崩，芬獻誄曰：
units.en: When Empress Yang Yan died, Zuo Fen offered a lament:
units.literal: When primal Empress Yang Yuan died, Fen presented a dirge, saying:

units.zh: 惟泰始十年秋七月丙寅，晉元皇后楊氏崩，嗚呼哀哉！
units.en: On the bingyin day of the seventh month, in autumn of the tenth Taishi year (274), Jin’s Empress Yang Yan passed—alas!
units.literal: On the bingyin day of autumn in the seventh month of the tenth Taishi year the Jin primal empress Lady Yang died—alas!

units.zh: 昔有莘適殷，姜姒歸周，宣德中闈，徽音永流。
units.en: Youxin wed Yin; Jiang and Si married into Zhou—inner chambers rang with virtue.
units.literal: Ancient Youxin married Yin; Jiang and Si married into Zhou—virtue spread within the palace, fair fame forever flows.

units.zh: 樊衛二姬，匡齊翼楚；
units.en: Fan Ji and Wei Ji uplifted Qi and Chu;
units.literal: The two Ji ladies of Fan and Wei steadied Qi and aided Chu;

units.zh: 馬鄧兩妃，亦毗漢主。
units.en: Ma and Deng consorts beside Han sovereigns did the same.
units.literal: the two consorts Ma and Deng likewise aided Han sovereigns.

units.zh: 峨峨元后，光嬪晉宇。
units.en: Towering primal queen—you lit the Jin harem.
units.literal: Lofty primal queen—you glorified consorts of Jin.

units.zh: 伉儷聖皇，比蹤往古。
units.en: You walked beside the sage throne as queens of old.
units.literal: You matched the sage emperor—tracks aligned with ancient models.

units.zh: 遭命不永，背陽即陰。
units.en: Heaven refused long life—you crossed from light to shade.
units.literal: Heaven granted no long span—you turned from yang toward shade.

units.zh: 六宮號咷，四海慟心。
units.en: Six wings of the harem keened; all beneath Heaven tore their breasts.
units.literal: Six palaces wailed; four seas shared torn hearts.

units.zh: 嗟余鄙妾，銜恩特深。
units.en: Mean concubine though I am—your kindness pierced deepest.
units.literal: Alas, mean concubine—I bore uniquely deep grace.

units.zh: 追慕三良，甘心自沈。
units.en: I envy the Three Worthies—I would gladly sink myself.
units.literal: I chase the Three Worthies—gladly I would sink myself.

units.zh: 何用存思？
units.en: Why hoard longing?
units.literal: What use is longing?

units.zh: 不忘德音。
units.en: Keep your virtuous words alive.
units.literal: Never forget virtuous words.

units.zh: 何用紀述？
units.en: Why record deeds?
units.literal: What use is chronicling?

units.zh: 託辭翰林。
units.en: Commit them to ink and Hanlin.
units.literal: Entrust phrases to the brush grove.

units.zh: 乃作誄曰：
units.en: Thus runs her lament:
units.literal: Thus she composed the dirge, saying:

units.zh: 赫赫元后，出自有楊。
units.en: Bright primal queen—you rose from the house of Yang.
